description: a codebase: a chief, an integrator, owners per area, a reviewer and a janitor, coordinating through the board and the spec
next: Next: /fleet up --dry-run (the plan, the lints and the cost), then /fleet up Chief and answer its interview with /fleet as its questions come. It drafts the charter, the roster and the shared files as changes for you to apply (/fleet <n> apply); then /fleet up --wave 1. The roster gives the instances auto mode ("settings" at its top), so they work with nobody at them: /fleet up --dry-run says each one's mode, and marks one that would ask. The chief drafts outbound.json too (your own hosts, remotes and addresses: sends there need no draft); later, /fleet <n> send --allow adds one as it goes. In a git repository, /fleet up --dry-run marks the instances a background session would move into a worktree copy (the README's Worktrees section).
